# Sercha

> A governed platform for querying documents like a database. You declare a
> schema (entities and edges) over a document corpus in SerchaQL, extraction
> populates it from documents in the source system, and you query the resulting
> graph with SQL-like syntax. Every read is permission-bounded at execution and
> written to a hash-chained audit log.

Sercha is a commercial product, self-hosted by the customer. It runs as a Go
binary against PostgreSQL with pgvector, OpenSearch for lexical search, and
OpenFGA for per-document authorization. Documents are read in place from the
connected source system rather than copied into a new store.

Key concepts:

- **Ontology**: a schema namespace. Mutable draft until bound.
- **Entity**: a typed object within an ontology. Behaves like a table once
  extracted. `KEY` marks resolution identity, not a uniqueness constraint.
- **Edge**: a named directed relationship, resolved at extraction time by exact
  match or LLM judgement.
- **Corpus**: a set of documents claimed from a source path.
- **Binding**: joins a corpus to an ontology and freezes an immutable version.
  `RUN BINDING` triggers extraction.

Every SerchaQL statement kind (DDL, DCL, DML, SHOW, DESCRIBE, EXPLAIN,
RUN BINDING) goes through one endpoint: `POST /api/v1/query`.

## Docs

- [What SerchaQL is](https://docs.sercha.dev/serchaql/intro): core concepts, the
  four nouns, and the three-layer permission model.
- [DDL reference](https://docs.sercha.dev/serchaql/ddl): every schema, binding
  and access-control statement.
- [DML reference](https://docs.sercha.dev/serchaql/dml): SELECT, edge traversal
  joins, search, aggregation, window functions and set operations.
- [A worked example](https://docs.sercha.dev/serchaql/example): a document
  corpus taken end to end, from schema declaration to a granted query.
- [API reference](https://docs.sercha.dev/api/sercha-enterprise-api): the full
  REST surface, generated from the OpenAPI spec.

## Optional

- [Execute a SerchaQL statement](https://docs.sercha.dev/api/execute-a-sercha-ql-statement):
  the single query endpoint, with request and response schemas.
